title: Rice hispid beetle on rice - Zambia

Header: Rice hispid beetle on rice - Zambia
Trichispa sericea Simomo in Lozi language

Prevention: January, before the outbreak of beetles.
Follow the plant's recommended spacing of 5cm x 30cm to avoid overcrowding of plants.
Remove alternative hosts like grassy weeds to reduce beetle food both in the field and field borders.
Rotate with a legume crop such as beans or cowpeas to break the pest life cycle.
Avoid the application of broad- spectrum insecticides as much as possible to protect natural enemies of the pest.
Apply balanced crop nutrition and avoid applying excessive doses of nitrogenous fertilisers.
Monitoring: This pest is most problematic during seedbed and early growth stages.
Look for dead rice plants both in nurseries and the main field due to chewing of leaf tissue by both larvae and adult beetles.
Look for small (5mm) shiny, blue-black beetles with short spines on the body.
Check every 2 weeks for mines on leaves and up to 6mm long pale yellow larvae in these mines.
Consider yellow direct control measures when 10-20 adult beetles and/or larvae are noticed per 10m2.
Direct Control: Handpick and destroy adult beetles; also you may use a sweep net to collect adult beetles.
Flood the rice fields, particularly during early crop stages, to chase away beetles by making their habitat unfavourable.
Place 5 blue medium-sized containers per lima filled with water and 2-5 teaspoons of soap (such as boom) to attract and kill the pest by drowning.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide (even a botanical home-brew), always wear protective clothing.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, and restricted re-entry interval.

Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (ZEMA).
Do not mix, spray, or clean containers near rivers as it is toxic to aquatic organisms (fish).
Apply when the crop is at the seedling stage.
Do not spray on flowering plants or near bee hives as it is toxic to bees.
Do not spray more than once in the season as it persists.
